Tilvar

Overview

Tilvar commands the guards in the governor’s city on Ingos. He serves Valrasian’s interests and discourages Zak from pursuing the missing Princess. The arrow found in a murdered investigator gives him a pretext for action against the Woodsfolk. His later advice about the sealed mines is useful, but he openly resents an outsider who might outshine his officers. [1, 2, 3]

Arrival on Ingos and the missing Princess

On Ingos, Zak first crosses the hostile countryside to reach the city. Tilvar tells him about the missing young woman known locally as the Princess and the reward offered for finding her. Governor Valrasian takes a personal interest in her, while Diera discourages the search. The hunter Sver the Trapper provides a concrete lead: another investigator, the Snoop from the capital, had followed the same trail before disappearing east of the city. Finding his body changes the search for a missing girl into an investigation of murder. [4, 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 2]

The arrow and the Green Clan

The arrow in the Snoop’s body appears to implicate the Woodsfolk. Sver explains that their markings identify a clan, while the governor discovers that the case containing similar arrows has been stolen from his collection. Two lines of inquiry now run alongside each other: the stolen collection and the Woodsfolk’s testimony. To approach Grey Leaf, Zak first returns the Green Clan’s Sacred Flower after rescuing its keeper from the White Clan. Grey Leaf then asks for help with the kidnapped elder Khabburu and his captor. The clan ultimately identifies the murder arrow as a false attribution, even refusing to blame its enemies for it. When the clan moves, Zak receives access to its hidden route and new home. [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]

Karansul’s accounts and Baldie’s confession

Karansul first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends Trickster as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find Flein the Baldie, called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. [15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22]

Diera and the locked mines

At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries. [23, 24, 25, 3, 26, 27, 28, 29]
